detail:
StatPearls describes celiac artery compression syndrome, also known as Dunbar syndrome or median arcuate ligament syndrome (MALS), as a rare medical condition characterized by recurrent abdominal pain. The condition results from compression of the celiac artery by a fibrous band of the diaphragm known as the median arcuate ligament, which connects the two medial borders of the diaphragmatic crura, usually near the level of the 12th thoracic or first lumbar vertebra. Lipshutz first reported the anatomical compression in 1917; as a clinical entity, the syndrome was first described by Harjola in 1963, and Dunbar described the first clinical study in 1965.

The reported incidence is 2 per 100,000 population, and the condition is commonly seen in young females between the ages of 30 to 50 years, with a female-to-male ratio of 4 to 1. The etiology is not fully understood: the same anatomic compression can be seen in people with no symptoms, and radiographic compression of the celiac axis has been reported in 10% to 24% of some populations, while symptomatic compression exists in a much smaller percentage. Patients may complain of epigastric abdominal pain, typically after food intake, along with anorexia, diarrhea, nausea, and a decline in weight over time, and examination may reveal mild epigastric tenderness or an abdominal bruit.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about median arcuate ligament syndrome symptoms and evaluation.
summary: StatPearls describes median arcuate ligament syndrome, also called celiac artery compression syndrome or Dunbar syndrome, as a rare condition of recurrent abdominal pain caused by compression of the celiac artery by a fibrous band of the diaphragm, reported in about 2 per 100,000 people.
takeaways: mals is compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament
reported incidence is about 2 per 100,000; most often women ages 30 to 50
the same compression appears in people with no symptoms
pain typically follows meals and can come with weight loss
title: Median arcuate ligament syndrome: a ligament pressing on the celiac artery
